mise () 
{ 
    local command;
    command="${1:-}";
    if [ "$#" = 0 ]; then
        command "$__MISE_EXE";
        return;
    fi;
    shift;
    case "$command" in 
        deactivate | shell | sh)
            if [[ ! " $* " =~ " --help " ]] && [[ ! " $* " =~ " -h " ]]; then
                eval "$(command "$__MISE_EXE" "$command" "$@")";
                return $?;
            fi
        ;;
    esac;
    command "$__MISE_EXE" "$command" "$@"
}

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Considering what a fifth personality letter could represent, beyond the traditional four dimensions.

A fifth letter could encode proprietary dimensions like stress behavior and faith. Existing five-letter personality systems will be noted for reference without copying them.

Assertive versus Turbulent is a proprietary fifth axis, but it should not be copied directly. Cognitive functions and stress models are separate from letter systems. Proprietary candidates include stress response pairs such as Calm versus Under-pressure, or Withdraw versus Surge. Faith-based dimensions like Reach-for-God versus Reach-for-control are also possible, though sensitive.

Other candidate axes include energy under load versus rest preference, certainty versus ambiguity tolerance, pace, conflict style, change orientation, and social behavior under stress.

Adding a fifth letter makes thirty-two possible types. Product naming must remain honest and avoid cloning existing systems. This remains advisory unless the user wants direct edits.
</details></think>

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Yes. Four letters = 16 stacks. Fifth binary letter = **32** stacks. Math is easy. Hard part: pick an axis you actually own, write your own questions, don't ship someone else's fifth letter as dress-up.

**Fit your proprietary gap best**

| Candidate | Pair (examples) | Why |
|-----------|-----------------|-----|
| Stress style | Withdraw / Surge | Matches "type talk without how you act under stress" |
| Stress style | Freeze / Fix | Same gap, more action-flavored |
| Stress style | Blame / Own | Character under pressure; faith-adjacent |
| Pressure faith | Reach / Control | Prayer/trust vs grip-the-wheel - careful, optional mode |
| Rest vs load | Easy-day / Hard-day | Same person, two modes - letter marks the *load* profile |

**Other solid fifth axes (less tied to your gap)**

| Candidate | Pair | Notes |
|-----------|------|-------|
| Certainty | Sure / Open | How fast you lock a belief |
| Conflict | Straight / Soft | How you fight |
| Pace | Rush / Wait | Tempo under normal life |
| Change | Keep / Shift | Habit vs reinvention |
| Social load | Crowd-ok / Crowd-tax | Not the same as outward/inward energy |
| Finish | Close / Leave | Related to plan/open, risk of overlap - only if you define it as *follow-through under boredom*, not J/P |

**Skip cloning**

Popular quiz sites already use a fifth letter for "assertive vs turbulent." That is **their** product surface. Same rule as nicknames: idea of a fifth axis is fine; their labels/items/scoring copy are not.

**Product choices**

1. Fifth letter always on (32 results)  
2. Fifth letter only in a "pressure mode" add-on (keeps core 16, proprietary layer separate)  
3. No letter - stress as a second score line under the four-letter map (simpler for high schoolers)

For *your* thesis, strongest candidates: **Withdraw/Surge**, **Freeze/Fix**, or **Blame/Own**, with faith as optional flavor on the same pressure axis - not a sixth letter yet.

Want one of these written into the draft as the proprietary fifth letter?

**Question:** Does stewardship make sense as the fifth letter on this trait quiz?

---

### White / First Principles

Known: Four preference letters map energy, info, decisions, lifestyle. A fifth letter needs a binary preference that is observable, scorable from items, and mostly independent of the four. JoRap's garden already defines stewardship as **use vs bury / borrow vs own** for gifts after salvation - moral-spiritual posture, not a Jung-style preference. Stake: wrong fifth letter either clones a popular "assertive/turbulent" pattern, overlaps the four, or turns a curiosity quiz into a discipleship grade.

Unknown: Whether quiz is church-only, dual-mode, or general. Whether stewardship would be scored as trait preference or as formation aspiration. Checkable: Can you write 6–8 high-school items that sort people into Steward vs Owner without sounding like a sermon or Free Grace confusion?

---

### Red / Instinct

Stewardship is *you* - real JoRap DNA. Feels holy and sticky. Also feels like putting the sermon in the letter slot meant for "what you do when the room heats up." Gut: love it as flavor text; distrust it as the fifth letter.

---

### Black / Contrarian

It does **not** work cleanly as the fifth letter.

Stewardship in your notes is an ethic after the gospel, not a temperament switch. Pairing Steward / Owner (or Use / Bury) grades people: one side sounds virtuous, the other sounds sinful. Preference quizzes die when one pole is the "good Christian answer." High schoolers either fake Steward or feel judged. Free Grace risk: quiz results start sounding like "faithful enough," which your notes already warn against.

Also orthogonal-fail: under stress you wanted pressure behavior. Stewardship is about gifts/platform over time - different timescale than crisis. You'll dilute the proprietary stress gap you already named. And "stewardship" is not high-school plain without a Bible class.

---

### Yellow / Expansionist

If stewardship *were* the fifth letter in a church product, upside is huge brand coherence. Your garden already owns the language. Results pages write themselves: Rule Keeper + Steward vs Rule Keeper + Owner - borrowed talent used or buried. Ties faith thread and proprietary IP in one letter. Distinct from every clone quiz. For a DNPAP / small-group / notes-garden mode, thirty-two stacks become a discipleship conversation starter nobody else has. Naming honesty stays intact - fully yours.

---

### Green / Options

1. **Do nothing on stewardship-as-letter** - keep fifth letter on pressure (Slow/Rush or Script/Wing); put stewardship only in optional faith result blurbs.
2. **Stewardship as overlay, not letter** - after type + stress letter, one short "how do you treat what was entrusted?" reflection block - unscored or separately scored.
3. **Church-mode fifth letter only** - secular quiz uses pressure letter; faith mode swaps in Use/Bury - two products, one core sixteen.

---

### Outsider

You're building a personality quiz and asking if "stewardship" should be a letter. To a stranger that reads like a church values assessment wearing type-quiz clothes. Fine if the box says church tool. Confusing if the pitch is "build your own trait quiz without cloning." They'll ask: is this about how I think, or whether I'm a good steward?

Notes support both: pressure hub ([[Slow the Moment]], [[Control the Rhythm]]) vs finish hub ([[Finish Strong]], compounding). Stake: one proprietary fifth letter for v1 - wrong pick dilutes the post and the product.

---

### White / First Principles

Known: Two different constructs. Wait/Go = acute tempo under load (minutes–day). Perseverance = stay with a hard goal over time (weeks–years). Draft, sample items, and pairing section are already Wait/Go. Garden density for *pressure* notes is high; *finish* notes also real but answer a different fight. Unknown: primary user of the quiz (team under outages vs students finishing projects). Checkable: which collision do you actually want the letter to explain on Monday - Slack war-room vs abandoned side project?

---

### Red / Instinct

Wait/Go feels alive. Outages, group chats, family exit - blood in it. Perseverance feels like a report card word. Respect it. Don't want it as the sexy fifth letter.

---

### Black / Contrarian

Perseverance as fifth letter is the worse v1 pick **if** you keep the current draft thesis.

You already sold “type talk without how you act under stress.” Switching to Stick/Switch orphans the ten heat items, the pairing table, and the pressure-notes claim. Perseverance also virtue-grades harder: Stick = good student; Switch = flaky. High schoolers fake Stick. Wait/Go can be framed as two useful jobs.

Perseverance also overlaps “Plan Closer / Finish Lead” energy and [[Finish Strong]] without needing a new letter - four-letter map + habits already lean there. Heat Pace is the gap the four letters don't cover.

---

### Yellow / Expansionist

Perseverance wins the school/church/training market: stick with the course, the instrument, the long build. Gorgeous result copy. Heat Pace wins the builder/team market: who buys time vs who moves in the incident. If JoRap.com is a developer/personal-site brain, Heat Pace products write themselves (deploy night, client thread). Upside of staying: ship what the draft already is; own a niche clones don't use (they copy assertive/turbulent, not Wait/Go).

---

### Green / Options

1. **Do nothing / keep Wait/Go** - rename axis only (Load Tempo) if Heat Pace bugs you.  
2. **Switch fifth letter to Stick/Switch** - rewrite samples, pairing, practical section around long finish.  
3. **Wait/Go as letter; perseverance as unscored follow-up** - “Did you finish last quarter?” after the type result.

---

### Outsider

One quiz, two candidates: “how fast under stress” vs “do you persevere.” Stranger asks which problem the product solves. Draft already answers stress. Changing now looks like second-guessing, not strategy.

---

### Executor

Keep Wait/Go. Optionally rename Heat Pace → **Load Tempo** in the draft in one find-replace. Leave perseverance out of the fifth-letter slot.

---

### Self-review

1. Strongest: Black - thesis mismatch if you switch.  
2. Blind spot: if audience is mostly kids finishing schoolwork, Yellow’s perseverance case gets stronger.  
3. Missed: whether Plan/Open already eats perseverance enough to make Stick/Switch redundant.

### Blue / Chairman

## Where the lenses agree
They are different traits. V1 needs one. Draft and notes already lean acute pressure.

## Where the lenses clash
Yellow likes perseverance for long-haul markets; Black/Red/Outsider say that abandons the stress gap you claimed.

## Blind spots
Primary audience still soft. Default to the collision the practical section already writes (deploy, client, family rush).

## The recommendation
**Heat Pace (Wait/Go) is better for this quiz.** It fills the gap the four letters miss, matches your pressure notes, and the draft is already built for it. Perseverance is a strong *other* axis - not a better fifth letter here. If the name “Heat Pace” still bothers you, rename to **Load Tempo**; don’t swap the construct to Stick/Switch.

## The one thing to do first
Lock Wait/Go as the fifth letter; only decide whether to rename Heat Pace → Load Tempo.

A good fifth is (1) mostly independent of those four, (2) binary and scorable, (3) changes what you do with the same four-letter stack. Wait/Go = tempo when stakes spike *now*. Stick/Switch = stay with a long hard goal vs bail/change. Checkable orthogonality: can Quiet Planner be Wait *and* Stick? Yes. Can Idea Starter be Go *and* Switch? Yes. Unknown: which failure mode users hit more - acute collision under heat, or abandoned long projects. Applicability = how often the letter explains a real fight the four letters leave muddy.

---

### Red / Instinct

Wait/Go feels like the missing gear. Same type, different disaster - that click is satisfying. Perseverance feels important and also like something report cards already grade. Gut pick: Wait/Go.

---

### Black / Contrarian

Perseverance is the weaker complement to the four.

Plan/open already leans toward finish-vs-flex. Stick/Switch partly re-measures Judging-ish follow-through and conscientiousness cosplay. You get double-counting: Plan Closer + Stick ≈ “finisher” twice. Virtue tilt is worse: Stick sounds morally better; Switch sounds flaky - people fake Stick.

Wait/Go has its own bleed risk: outward energy + Go can correlate; inward + Wait can correlate. Still, calm E/I ≠ heat tempo - plenty of outward Wait (buy time out loud) and inward Go (silent hotfix). Fatal issue for perseverance: less new information per letter once J/P exists.

---

### Yellow / Expansionist

Wait/Go unlocks the best complementary story: **style × heat**. Sixteen types become thirty-two *behavior modes* under load - pairing, incident roles, family rush, without claiming new “personality.” Perseverance unlocks style × long game - gorgeous for school, training, creative careers. Market for Stick/Switch is huge (every coach wants finishers). If applicability means “parents and teachers,” perseverance wins the poster. If applicability means “explains fights the four letters can’t,” Wait/Go wins the lab.

---

### Green / Options

1. **Do nothing** - no fifth letter; teach stress/finish as unscored notes under each type.  
2. **Wait/Go as fifth** - acute tempo; leave perseverance to habits/process.  
3. **Stick/Switch as fifth** - long finish; leave heat to coaching scripts.

---

### Outsider

You have four “how I prefer to be” switches. Adding “do you persevere?” sounds like sneaking a character grade into a preference quiz. Adding “when it hits the fan, do you pause or push?” sounds like a fifth preference about conditions - stranger buys that faster as *complement*, not sermon.

---

### Executor

Choose Wait/Go as the complementary fifth. Define poles as Wait/Go under load only; write items that are useless on a calm Tuesday.

---

### Self-review

1. Strongest: Black - J/P overlap kills perseverance as complement.  
2. Blind spot: teen/school context could still want Stick/Switch more than builders do.  
3. Missed: a third complement (Own/Blame under heat) - out of scope for “among the two.”

---

### Blue / Chairman

## Where the lenses agree
Fifth letter must add what the four don’t. Both candidates are real traits; only one complements cleanly.

## Where the lenses clash
Yellow’s school/coach market loves perseverance; Black/Outsider say it overlaps plan/open and moralizes.

## Blind spots
Audience mix unset - default to complementarity math, not draft sunk cost (per your zero-base ask).

## The recommendation
**Wait/Go (under-fire tempo) is better** - more complementary to the four, more applicable to collisions the four leave unexplained, less redundant with plan/open. Perseverance matters, but it partly re-asks Judging/finishing; as a fifth letter it grades virtue and double-counts. The four describe calm preference; the fifth should flip the *condition* (heat), not re-score the long report card.

## The one thing to do first
Lock the fifth construct as **Wait vs Go under load** - name the axis later (Load Tempo / Heat Pace / Pressure Pace); do not make perseverance the fifth letter.

Like the other four: a preference switch. Not a moral grade.

### The four (calm conditions)

| Switch | Plain question |
|--------|----------------|
| Energy | Refill with people, or alone? |
| Info | Trust facts in front of you, or patterns in your head? |
| Decide | Sort by head, or by heart? |
| Plan | Want it settled, or keep options open? |

Those four answer: **how you like to run when the room is normal.**

### The fifth: Wait / Go (under-fire tempo)

| Switch | Plain question |
|--------|----------------|
| **Heat** | When stakes spike, do you **buy a beat** (Wait), or **move now** (Go)? |

Same person. Different condition. The clock, the angry chat, the site down, someone yelling you're late.

- **Wait** - one breath, clarify “done,” lower the voice, answer by 3pm instead of now. Take tempo back.
- **Go** - reply while the thread is hot, hotfix while talking, grab the keys and fix details in motion. Let urgency take the first step.

Neither is “braver.” **Wait** without a deadline becomes freeze. **Go** without a check becomes a mess. Both are useful jobs under fire.

### Why add it?

The four don’t ask about **load**. Two Quiet Planners can share the same four letters and still fight:

- one wants a reproduce step and a rollback tab (**Wait**)
- one wants the patch live during the call (**Go**)

Without a fifth letter you call that “personality clash” or “doesn’t care.” With Wait/Go you name the real mismatch: **calm style matches; heat tempo doesn’t.**

So:

- Four letters = preferred style on an easy Tuesday  
- Fifth letter = tempo when Tuesday catches fire  

That’s why it was added - not grit, not perseverance, not “who volunteers first.” Only: **under fire, pause or push?**

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Short version: the four weren’t picked at random. They come from a long public line of “how people prefer to take in the world and act on it” - then got locked into four binary switches because that math gives sixteen useful stacks.

### Where they come from

1. **Jung** talked about how people differ in attention and judgment (extraversion/introversion, and ways of perceiving/judging).
2. Later popular systems (including the branded quiz you don’t want to clone, and books like *Please Understand Me*) turned that into **four everyday preference pairs**.
3. Builders kept those four because they’re **broad, scorable, and complementary** - each asks a different question.

Your draft already uses that public map. You didn’t invent the four; you inherited the shape, then added **Urgency**.

### Why these four (what each one is for)

| Switch | Everyday question | Why it earned a slot |
|--------|-------------------|----------------------|
| **Energy** (outward / inward) | Where do I refill? | Almost every group fight hits “why won’t they talk / why won’t they leave me alone.” |
| **Info** (facts / patterns) | What do I trust first? | Same meeting: one wants the checklist, one wants the “what if.” |
| **Decide** (head / heart) | What filter wins the hard call? | Logic-fairness vs people-impact - different “fair,” same team. |
| **Plan** (settled / open) | Do I want it locked or alive? | Deadlines vs options - calendar and packing-bag preference. |

Together they cover **social fuel → attention → decision filter → lifestyle tempo** without fully repeating each other.

### Why four (not three, not six)

- **Four binaries → 16 stacks** - enough variety to feel personal, not so many that nobody remembers the map.
- Each pair is meant to be a **preference under normal conditions**, not a skill grade.
- Gaps those four leave (on purpose): **acute urgency**, long perseverance, conflict style, etc. That’s why your fifth switch (**Urgency**) fits - it answers a question the four don’t ask.

### What they are *not*

- Not “the only true human traits”
- Not a full personality theory
- Not proof one side is better
- Not owned as ideas - **wording and item banks** of branded instruments are what’s locked down

### Tie to your quiz

You keep the four because readers already know that map and it still works for team talk. You add Urgency because two people can match on all four and still clash when the clock hits.

If you want, next step can be a short draft paragraph under “Five switches” that says this history in JoRap voice - why the four, then why Urgency.

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Short answer: the classic four were built as a closed set. People kept proposing fifths later. Some got popular; none became the “official” fifth of that branded system.

### Did *they* disregard a fifth?

Myers/Briggs-style four pairs were designed as **four**. Not “we almost shipped five and cut one.”

What got left outside the letter box:

| Idea | Why it didn’t become the fifth letter |
|------|----------------------------------------|
| Full Jung **function stack** (Ni, Te, etc.) | Richer model - not one clean binary preference |
| **Temperament** groups (Keirsey-style) | Collapses 16 into 4 families - different cut, not a fifth switch |
| **Emotional stability / anxiety** (Big Five neuroticism) | Real trait; feels like a grade (“calm vs fragile”); branded MBTI stayed preference-framed |
| **Strength / skill** | Preferences ≠ competence |

So: not one famous discarded fifth letter on a whiteboard. More like **whole other maps** that never became letter five.

### Fifths people *do* invent (common)

| Candidate | Poles (examples) | Obvious? | Problem |
|-----------|------------------|----------|---------|
| **Identity under stress** (popular quiz sites) | Assertive / Turbulent | Very - already cloned everywhere | Easy to moralize; their branding/items aren’t yours |
| **Emotional steadiness** | Steady / Reactive | Obvious if you know Big Five | Sounds like “who’s the mess” |
| **Conflict** | Direct / Soft | Useful on teams | Overlaps decide (head/heart) and your Urgency |
| **Pace of change** | Keep / Shift | Feels obvious | Overlaps plan/open |
| **Long finish** | Stick / Switch | Obvious for school/work | Overlaps plan/open + habits; virtue tilt |
| **Under-fire tempo** | Wait / Go (**your Urgency**) | Less cloned as a letter | Best complement to the calm four |
| **Social under load** | Crowd-ok / Crowd-tax | Related to energy | Easy to double-count E/I |

### What’s the *obvious* extra switch?

If “obvious” = what outsiders add first:

1. **Assertive / Turbulent-style** (confidence vs self-doubt under pressure) - market already did this  
2. **Steady / Reactive** (emotional stability) - psychologists point here when comparing to Big Five  

If “obvious” = what best **complements** the four without repeating them:

→ **Urgency (Wait / Go)** - condition change (calm → heat), not another calm lifestyle pole  

That’s why your pick is less “default internet fifth” and more “fills the real hole.”

### Practical takeaway

- Classic four: no official disregarded fifth letter - just a four-slot design.  
- Obvious cloned fifth: anxiety/confidence under stress.  
- Obvious *useful* fifth for teams: how you move when it gets urgent - what you already call **Urgency**.

**Big Five** and **MBTI-style** answer different jobs. One is trait science’s default map. The other is a preference sorting tool people use for talk and teams.

### Side by side

| | **Big Five (OCEAN)** | **MBTI-style (four pairs → 16)** |
|--|----------------------|----------------------------------|
| **What it is** | Five continuous traits | Four preference binaries (+ your Urgency would make five) |
| **Output** | Scores on a spectrum (you can be “medium”) | Letter stack / type label |
| **Core claim** | Stable dimensions of personality | Preferred ways of attending and deciding |
| **Best at** | Research, prediction, nuance | Shared language, pairing, workshops |
| **Weak at** | Catchy team nicknames | Science rigor / hiring validity |
| **Moral trap** | Lower Neuroticism often reads “better” | Each pole can pretend to be “the good one” if you let it |

### The five Big Five traits

| Trait | Plain meaning |
|-------|----------------|
| **O** Openness | New ideas, novelty, imagination |
| **C** Conscientiousness | Order, follow-through, duty |
| **E** Extraversion | Outward energy, social drive |
| **A** Agreeableness | Cooperation, soft vs hard with people |
| **N** Neuroticism | Stress reactivity, worry, mood swings |

(Often flipped as **Emotional Stability** = low N.)

### Rough overlap (not 1:1)

| MBTI-style switch | Closest Big Five | Fit |
|-------------------|------------------|-----|
| Energy (E/I) | Extraversion | Strongest overlap |
| Info (S/N) | Openness (partly) | Loose - N ≠ “creative genius” |
| Decide (T/F) | Agreeableness (partly) | Loose - T/F is decision filter, not niceness |
| Plan (J/P) | Conscientiousness (partly) | Loose - J ≠ always “more responsible” |
| *(no classic pair)* | **Neuroticism** | Big gap - Big Five has it; classic four don’t |
| Your **Urgency (Wait/Go)** | Not the same as N | Tempo under load ≠ “how anxious you are” |

### Key differences

**1. Spectrum vs box**  
Big Five: you’re 62% Extraversion.  
MBTI-style: you’re E or I (even if you’re near the middle).

**2. Personality vs preference framing**  
Big Five owns “personality traits.”  
Your draft’s better frame: **preferences** - closer to how MBTI *markets* itself, even when people treat types as destiny.

**3. What’s missing where**  
- Classic MBTI-style map underplays **stress reactivity** (Neuroticism). That’s why Assertive/Turbulent clones showed up.  
- Big Five underplays a clean **under-fire tempo** story (Wait/Go) as a team pairing tool.

**4. Use case**  
- Want research / prediction → Big Five.  
- Want “two Plan Closers fighting on deadline night” language → preference map (+ Urgency).

### For your quiz

Don’t claim Big Five science. Don’t clone MBTI. You’re building a **preference map**: four calm switches + Urgency. Big Five is the foil that explains why people ask for a fifth about anxiety - and why your fifth (tempo under urgency) is a different, team-useful cut.

- Keep nuance (scores, not boxes)
- Speak the language of psychology science

**Give people a shared language for how they prefer to work and decide** so teams can talk and pair without needing a lab.

- Sort calm preferences into memorable stacks
- Make differences discussable (“facts first” vs “patterns first”)
- Support workshops, self-reflection, team talk
- (In your version) add Urgency so heat fights get named, not moralized

### Goal clash in one line

| | Big Five | Preference map |
|--|----------|----------------|
| Primary goal | **Explain/predict personality** | **Coordinate preferences** |
| Unit of success | Accurate measurement | Useful conversation |
| Output people want | Profile scores | Type / stack label |
| Failure mode | Overclaim from weak data | Treat preference as destiny |

### For your draft

Your goal matches the **preference map**: don’t clone a brand, own Urgency, no best pole, team pairing.  
Big Five’s goal is adjacent but different - useful as contrast (“science map vs team map”), not as the thing you’re shipping.

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user wants to build a Big Five personality assessment without copyright issues.

The Big Five framework itself is not trademarked. Specific instruments like NEO-PI-R and NEO-FFI carry copyright. IPIP items have various licenses. The International Personality Item Pool offers public domain alternatives.

IPIP items are often freely available for research and non-commercial use with attribution. Commercial instruments such as NEO contain proprietary scoring keys and manuals that must not be copied. Construct ideas are not copyrightable, so designing original items is generally safe. The term "Big Five" is somewhat generic, though specific product names may still be trademarked. This remains general guidance, not legal advice.
</details></think>

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

**Short answer:** You can build a **Big Five–*style*** quiz more cleanly than cloning MBTI - if you write **your own items** (or use a **known free item pool** with its license). You still cannot copy a commercial test’s questions, manual, or scoring key.

Not legal advice. Product hygiene.

### What’s usually free to use as *ideas*

| Piece | Clone risk |
|-------|------------|
| The five traits (OCEAN / similar plain names) | Low - scientific constructs, widely used |
| “People differ on five continuous scales” | Low - idea, not owned text |
| Your own agree/disagree items that aim at those traits | Low - if wording is original |
| Your own product name | Fine if it doesn’t copy a brand |

### What’s locked / risky

| Piece | Risk |
|-------|------|
| **NEO-PI-R / NEO-FFI** (and similar commercial batteries) items, manuals, keys | High - copyrighted instruments |
| Copying any paid “Big Five test” question bank | High |
| Using their exact scale names + marketing as “the official Big Five” | Trademark / false association risk |
| Publishing someone else’s PDF “for free” | High |

### Cleaner paths

1. **Write your own items** in plain language for Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Emotional Stability (or Neuroticism). Score continuous (Likert). Own the product name.  
2. **Use IPIP** ([International Personality Item Pool](https://ipip.ori.org/)) - community item pool built so researchers aren’t stuck only on commercial tests. **Read the license on the scales you pick** (attribution / use limits vary by scale). Don’t assume “Big Five = public domain.”  
3. **Cite the model**, don’t pretend you’re Costa/McCrae’s instrument.

### Vs MBTI clone risk

| | MBTI-style | Big Five–style |
|--|------------|----------------|
| Branded instrument culture | Heavy (name, items, type pages) | Heavier on **specific tests** (NEO etc.), lighter on the OCEAN idea itself |
| Type labels / 16 nicknames | Easy to stumble into brand dress | Less “type nickname” trap |
| Safe DIY | Own wording + own name | Own wording + own name (or licensed IPIP) |

### For *your* project

- **Yes**, you can ship a no-clone Big Five–*shaped* quiz if items (and name) are yours or properly licensed.  
- **Still** don’t copy NEO (or any commercial) items.  
- Your current draft’s goal (team preference + Urgency pairing) still fits the **preference map** better than Big Five. Big Five’s goal is trait measurement - different job.

If you want both: preference map for teams, optional separate “five scales” quiz with original items - two products, two goals.

| Preference pair (16-type map) | Closest Big Five |
|------------------------------|------------------|
| Energy (E/I) | Extraversion |
| Info (S/N) | Openness (loose) |
| Decide (T/F) | Agreeableness (loose) |
| Plan (J/P) | Conscientiousness (loose) |
| **(missing)** | **Neuroticism / Emotional Stability** |

So if you want “Big Five’s leftover” as a fifth switch, it’s the stress-reactivity one - not Openness (already kinda in S/N) or Conscientiousness (kinda in J/P).

Popular quiz sites’ Assertive/Turbulent is basically this hole dressed as a letter.

### Can you “merge Big Five into 16 types”?

| Approach | What you get | Honesty check |
|----------|--------------|---------------|
| **Correlate** | Research: types lean higher/lower on OCEAN | Fine as “rough cousins,” not identity |
| **Fifth letter = Steady / Reactive** | 16 → 32, Big-Five-flavored | Closest true merge of the *missing* trait |
| **Score OCEAN under each type** | Type label + 5 meters | Two systems glued; heavy UX |
| **Replace 16 with Big Five only** | No types | Different product |

You cannot honestly say “ISTJ = these exact Big Five scores.” Overlap is partial. Boxes ≠ spectra.

### Steady/Reactive vs your Urgency (Wait/Go)

| | **Steady / Reactive** (Big Five N) | **Wait / Go** (your Urgency) |
|--|-------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| Asks | How much does stress shake me? | When it is urgent, pause or push? |
| Feel | Mood / worry / recovery | Tempo / first move under load |
| Team use | “Who needs buffer when heat rises” | “Who buys time vs who moves first” |
| Virtue trap | Reactive sounds “worse” | Easier to frame as two useful jobs |
| Fit to “no best answer” | Harder | Easier |

Same heat, different cut. A Reactive-Wait and a Steady-Go are different people.

### Practical recommendation

- **Want Big Five’s missing piece as fifth letter** → Steady / Reactive (Emotional Stability).  
- **Want best complement for team pairing + no best pole** → keep **Urgency (Wait/Go)**.  
- **Want both** → don’t mash into one letter. Options:  
  - Urgency as the letter (32 types)  
  - Steady/Reactive as a **separate meter** under the result (Big Five–style, continuous)

Merging “all of Big Five into 16 types” as one alphabet usually becomes mush. One fifth trait from Big Five is doable - and that trait is almost always **Neuroticism / Emotional Stability**.
